newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:
* Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston withdrew his name from consideration to become chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff amidst a furor over his acknowledged adulterous affair in the mid-1980s.
* U.S. Rep. Bill Archer, R-Texas, outlined a series of federal tax cuts.
* New York State's battle over rent-control laws now centers on whether landlords should be allowed to raise rents as much as they want on regulated apartments that become vacant.

* Investigators now say they have linked bombings that took place at a lesbian nightclub and at a building housing an abortion clinics, and are increasingly confident those Atlanta bombings may also be connected to the explosion at the Summer Olympics.
* Cablevision Systems Corp plans to buy local cable television systems that have more than 820,000 customers in the New York area from Tele-Communications Inc.

* China has purchased several dozen American-made supercomputers, making some U.S. government officials concerned that they could be used to build more efficient nuclear weapons that could reach the United States.
